meta.description: Lore Talents (Wissens-Talente) from TDE 4.1. These talents represent specialized knowledge. Tests may be rolled secretly by the Highlord. Contested tests are unusual in this category; remaining TP often determine the quality and breadth of knowledge. Encumbrance is generally negligible unless there is a 'craft' aspect. Advancement column B.

talents.name: Anatomy
talents.description: The science of bodies, their internal relationships and structure — a foundational science for the healing arts. Since this knowledge can only be gained from corpses or convicted criminals, the profession of anatomist is not highly regarded, and in many places is even forbidden. However, a well-trained anatomist can immediately recognize serious wounds and certain types of organ diseases, easing corresponding Treat Wounds tests by half the Anatomy TP. They also know the most vulnerable points of the human body and cause 1 additional TP in unarmed combat with Anatomy TP of at least 10. Cannot take the Fear of the Dead disadvantage. Note: bonuses from Anatomy and Butcher do not stack.

talents.name: Appraise
talents.description: When one finds a small ring or a golden goblet in an abandoned tomb, there's no price tag on it. After a successful Appraise test, the Highlord tells the hero what price they could roughly get for an item. When shopping at the market, a test helps recognize the true value of overpriced goods. The Highlord may roll secretly. Note: the Appraise talent applies only to monetary values, not to assessing distances, required building materials, etc. (other talents handle those).

talents.name: Arcane Lore
talents.description: What will happen next when the Alanfanian sorcerer makes a fist? Could this scintillating ring be an old lizardfolk artifact? Why do the elf's tracks end abruptly as if he vanished into thin air? All these questions can be answered by anyone (not just a magician) who has devoted some time to studying the arcane arts. This talent is one of the magician's most important tools of the trade. Requires Read/Write of a suitable cultural language at TP 6 to advance beyond TP 10.

talents.name: Board Games
talents.description: Knowledge of the most important board games (such as Urdas, Garadan, the Thorwalian Hneftafl, or the widely varied Tulamidyan camel game) as well as card games (notably the widespread Boltan or Fünfas game). This talent encompasses not only the rules but also playing technique, combinations, position assessment, and similar skills.

talents.name: Calculate
talents.description: Like Read/Write, actual tests using this talent will be rare during play. TP 0: can count but not calculate; distinguishes between many/few and more/less. TP 1-2: counting and calculating is laborious, requires fingers and toes. TP 3: reasonable command of basic arithmetic. TP 4+: prerequisite for tests in many other fields of study. TP 6+: the really arcane topics (geometry, calculating roots, compound interest, basics of calculus) begin to become accessible.

talents.name: Engineering
talents.description: Knowledge of Engineering can be useful in many situations. This talent covers knowledge of basic physical principles: lever laws, friction, block and tackle, inclined planes, and similar. If the hero wants to construct improvised mechanical devices (e.g., room traps, catapult devices, or block-and-tackle systems), a successful Engineering test proves the functionality of the device. The more complex the device, the higher the difficulty increase. Knowledge of fine mechanics (precision engineering, locks, lock traps, musical clocks) falls under the Light Engineering (Feinmechanik) artisan talent. The Highlord may roll secretly; functional tests are revealed on first use. Requires Calculate 6, Paint/Draw 6, and Read/Write 6 to advance beyond TP 10.

talents.name: Geography
talents.description: Regional knowledge — a subject one can laboriously memorize from writings or learn quasi-automatically from wide travels, practical experience being far preferable to the theoretical. On a successful Geography test, the Highlord provides the hero with relevant geographical facts (landscape features, climate, soil type, navigable rivers, passable passes, etc.). High Geography TP also provides basic knowledge of the inhabitants of a region, but detailed cultural questions require the appropriate Kulturkunde special ability.

talents.name: Heraldry
talents.description: While the Etiquette talent covers general manners — especially at court — and includes incidental knowledge of coats-of-arms, Heraldry is devoted exclusively to the history, development, and spread of heraldic devices of all types: coats-of-arms, shield and field insignia, helm crests, banners, standards, and the like. Also covers the relationships between important noble houses and issues of lineage and inheritance. A hero with Heraldry can determine which province a knight is from, whether he is from a legitimately noble line, or whether a villain is using forged or invented heraldry. At higher TP, also provides knowledge of the colors and banners of regiments.

talents.name: History
talents.description: Aventuria's written history spans three thousand years, but the narratives of many peoples reach much further into the past. Since most heroes are regularly confronted with the history of their world — because they cannot let the dead lie in their graves — it is often useful to have a history-savvy companion nearby. History relies heavily on written sources; not only deciphering but also classifying and evaluating old texts is important for the knowledgeable historian. History can be complicated by lacking cultural knowledge. Requires Read/Write 4.

talents.name: Language Lore
talents.description: Knowing many languages is important for a merchant, but knowing a language does not help when encountering an obscure dialect, or stumbling across a tablet that looks 'vaguely Tulamidyan' but uses a different alphabet. Language Lore covers the relationships between known languages of the world, their development, branches, and their various written forms. The Highlord may allow tests when the hero knows a related language and wants to apply this to an unknown language, script, or dialect. Per 2 TP in Language Lore, the hero may learn one language of their choice. Language Lore is required to learn certain (ancient) foreign languages.

talents.name: Law
talents.description: This talent covers knowledge of legal procedures of various Aventurian nations and peoples, most prominently guild law, state law, criminal law, and church law of the Twelvegods. This is especially important for traveling heroes, since laws and regulations vary widely across the continent. Useful for dealing with all the inevitable hero-group infractions of local law (use of poison, insulting nobles and clergy, weapon laws). The Highlord may roll secretly; results are modified by Kulturkunde special abilities.

talents.name: Legend Lore
talents.description: Heroes versed in this talent are not only familiar with the customs and traditions of their own and other peoples, but can also identify specific gods and heroic figures and recount the most important sagas and legends of a people. Thus, this is not only a talent for diplomats and scholars, but also for traveling singers and storytellers. Tests on the widespread myths and legends of one's own culture are required only in exceptional cases. Knowing legends of foreign peoples requires appropriate Kulturkunde special ability, otherwise tests are made harder.

talents.name: Plant Lore
talents.description: The knowledgeable botanist not only knows where to find familiar plants but also how to assess strange and unknown plants, comparing them to known ones. The ability to extract poisons or medicines from plants is also governed by this talent. Tests can be required in three areas: finding plants, identifying them, and using them to brew elixirs. A failed test for plant-finding may simply mean no appropriate specimen grows nearby; failed identification or brewing tests can have more dire consequences. The Highlord may roll secretly.

talents.name: Religious Lore
talents.description: Knowledge of religious rites and doctrines of one's own faith. An absolute must for any cleric who doesn't want to attract unwelcome attention in the temple of a sibling deity. Also covers knowledge of divine myths and saints' legends, as well as proper forms of address and bows before a priest or priestess. Heroes who have become knowledgeable about their own faith (TP at least 7) may also branch out into other religions. Without the appropriate Kulturkunde, tests regarding foreign religions should be made harder.

talents.name: Starcraft
talents.description: Starcraft not only includes astrology as a means of prophesying and fortune-telling, but also applies to navigation by the stars, methods of determining time, cataloging heavenly phenomena, and theoretical knowledge of the movements of celestial bodies on which all of the above fields rest. Since good telescopes are as rare as they are expensive, this talent is usually reserved for those of great patience and sharp eyes. Requires Read/Write [Garethi or Tulamidya], Calculate, and Perception each at TP 6 to advance beyond TP 10.

talents.name: Stone Lore
talents.description: Training in this talent enables recognition of suitable rock types for construction purposes and also enables searching the ground for ore deposits or prospecting for precious metals and gemstones. Additionally provides basic knowledge of the material properties of various types of stone, ore, and gemstones. It is no surprise that most Aventurian dwarfs understand these matters almost instinctively.

talents.name: Warcraft
talents.description: Playing a brave role as a fighter in a battle is one thing — actually directing the battle itself is another. Troops must be moved, supplied, and motivated. The terrain and the enemy's tactical capabilities must be scouted. Equally important is choosing the right moment to act, as well as gaining the favor of the gods. Strategy, tactics, and the commander's on-the-spot decisions are all aspects of Warcraft. A hero wishing to command more than ten warriors in battle should have at least TP 7 in Warcraft.

talents.name: Animal Lore
talents.description: Solid knowledge of the distribution and behavior of the most common animal species is a basic requirement for successful hunting. An experienced Animal Loremaster can also assess previously unknown animals by comparing them to familiar species. Successful Animal Lore tests can identify a particular species, predict animal behavior, or (combined with Sneak tests and secure weapon handling) determine the outcome of a hunt.
